tightiso/eta0.0-0.9_pt30-40.note: Accepted open issue. |pull| > 5 in a high-statistics bin where the POG uncertainty is only 0.02-0.1 percent: our SF is 0.2-0.5 percent above the POG in the 30-50 GeV bins of this working point (confirmed by a fit-free counting cross-check in the ARC review). Not covered by our uncertainties: MC-template statistics (MC/data pairs = 0.44; the tight-ID test shows such an offset shrinks with MC statistics, not tested for isolation) and the run-mix difference to the POG (F late + G + H). Fits converge and the background, window and tag systematics are below 0.1 percent here.

isomu24/eta0.0-0.9_pt26-30.note: Accepted open issue (barrel) / matching effect (elsewhere). With the skill's matching (tag and probe bit 2 or 8) the IsoMu24 SF is 0.8-1.5 percent above the POG (weighted SF/POG 1.013 at 30-60 GeV). It is robust against the fit, mass window, background shape, pileup weights, tag pT, the run era and the event-level HLT requirement, but it is a matching effect: with tag and probe matched to the bit-2 (Iso) object only, SF/POG at 40-50 GeV is 1.000-1.001 for |eta| > 0.9, while the barrel stays +1.2 percent at all pT (cause open); bit 8 alone gives SF/POG 0.960-0.988. The probe object pT threshold matters below 30 GeV for the efficiencies but moves the SF by <= 0.7 percent. See summary.json filter_bits.measurement (definitions a-e) and object_pt_threshold_scan. Event-level filter-bit bias is negligible (4.6e-5 of matched probes).
